title: Naturality of the common-stage Koszul braiding
statement: Let l be prime, Ω an algebraic closure of Q_l, and X a scheme on whose residue fields l is invertible. In the common finite coefficient-stage category C of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], use the specified tensor T of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and common-stage Koszul braiding β of [def-sf-rational-common-tensor-symmetries]. For any M,M′,N,N′ in C and any f:M→M′ and g:N→N′, T(f,g) ≫ β(M′,N′).hom = β(M,N).hom ≫ T(g,f). This includes all localized arrows and does not impose site-perfectness.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.11, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; agent-written common-field representative argument, refining step 6 of lem-sf-adic-common-stage-hom-transpose.

proof.text: Integral braiding is the coherent-reduction-normalized Koszul symmetry. Naturality of that symmetry and the reduction/tensor comparison implies integral naturality: apply the faithful coherent reduction functor, substitute the defining normalization of both braidings, and cancel the reduction tensor comparisons. Localized tensor braiding naturality then extends this equation to arbitrary rational arrows.

Choose one finite common field containing representatives of f and g, all four object fields and all four tensor-object fields. Substitute the tensor map and braiding representative formulas, both conjugated by commonStageTensorComparison. Middle comparisons cancel. Rational braiding naturality proves equality at that field, hence equality of common-stage classes. These formulas hold at every enlarged field, so no scalar-extension Hom map is assumed injective.
